title: What Even Is Trading?
hook: Candles are just storytelling — they're showing you who's winning right now.
mission: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to look at a stretch of price and say who's currently in control — buyers or sellers — without guessing.

beats.heading: It's a disagreement
beats.body: Buyers think price should go higher. Sellers think price should go lower. That disagreement creates movement — that's it.

beats.heading: Not a prediction
beats.body: Everything you see on a chart is just that battle being printed in real time. You're reading current behavior, not seeing the future.

blocks.quote: If I can tell who has control, I already have a reason to be interested. I'm not trying to be psychic. I'm watching behavior.

blocks.heading: What did she get wrong?
blocks.scenario: A trader says she's "predicting the future" every time she takes a trade.

options.label: She's not predicting anything — she's reading current disagreement between buyers and sellers
options.feedback: Exactly. Trading reads present behavior — who's currently winning the disagreement — not a crystal ball.

options.label: Nothing — that's exactly what trading is
options.feedback: Not quite. Calling it "predicting the future" overstates what's actually happening on the chart.

blocks.heading: Read the story forward
blocks.prompt: What's the next logical read in this story — not where price goes, what does the behavior suggest?

options.label: Sellers are starting to contest the level buyers have been winning
options.feedback: Right — long upper wicks mean price reached higher but couldn't hold it. That's sellers showing up.

options.label: Nothing has changed — wicks don't mean anything
options.feedback: Wicks aren't nothing — they show price getting rejected from an area, which is real information.

questions.question: Price steps higher for ten candles, then prints one long-wicked red candle that closes back above the prior low. Has control actually shifted to sellers?
options: No — the close shows buyers reclaimed it before the candle ended
Yes — any long red wick means sellers won
It's impossible to tell from one candle
questions.why: Reading control means watching where price closes, not just where it traveled during the candle.

questions.question: In futures, your profit comes mainly from:
options: Price movement in the direction you chose
Owning a share of a company
questions.why: Futures profit is based on movement, not ownership — there's no company stake involved.

blocks.prompt: Imagine another AGHF girl asks: "Isn't trading just guessing?" How would you explain what's actually happening when you trade?

takeaways: Trading is buyers and sellers disagreeing on price — not fortune-telling.
A candle's close tells you who actually won that period, not just the wick.
Futures profit comes from movement, not ownership.
remember: You're not trying to be psychic. You're watching behavior.
